title: Yitro: named for an outsider
hookLine: the portion with the Ten Words is named for Jethro, a Midianite priest

lines: NAMED FOR A PRIEST OF MIDIAN.
cards: A trivia question. Which portion of the Torah holds the Ten Commandments, the moment at Mount Sinai, thunder, smoke, the voice of God? And what's it called?
Not Moses. Not Sinai. Not the Ten Words.
It's named after Moses' father-in-law, a priest of Midian, who wasn't an Israelite at all. His name was Jethro; in Hebrew, Yitro.
And before Sinai even comes into view, he walks into the camp and tells Moses he's doing his job wrong.

teach.b: Yitro has heard everything God did for Israel, and he comes to the wilderness bringing Moses' wife Zipporah and their two sons. Moses tells him the whole story, and Yitro rejoices, and blesses the God who rescued them.
The next morning he watches Moses sit as judge for the people, from morning until evening, everyone lining up with their disputes.

teach.h: THE THING THAT THOU DOEST IS NOT GOOD.
teach.b: And he says, in the old Jewish translation: "The thing that thou doest is not good." You'll wear yourself out, and the people too. Then a plan.
Make them judges over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens. Let them handle the small cases and bring you the great ones.
And Moses listens; he does what his father-in-law says. In the Torah's telling, Israel's courts are built on the advice of an outsider.
Rashi, quoting the old midrash, says Yitro had seven names, and one of them, Yeter, means addition, because he added a section to the Torah.

The rabbis even argued about the timing: did he come before Sinai, or after, with the Torah moving his story here? They didn't settle it. But there it sits, right before the Ten Words, and the portion carries his name.
A tradition that names the portion of Sinai after a Midianite priest is saying something about where wisdom can come from.

how: Yitro is read in synagogue in winter; when the Ten Commandments are chanted, people in some congregations stand. Jewish teachers point out that the portion is named for Jethro, a Midianite priest.

o: Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, a priest of Midian
a name for Mount Sinai, where the Ten Words came
a judge Moses set over a thousand of the people

games.q: who's who in Yitro's visit — tap the pairs.
p: Moses' wife, brought with her sons

s: the portion with the Ten Commandments is named for Moses
it's named Yitro, for Jethro, a priest of Midian.
he appointed judges over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens.

games.q: your father-in-law, a priest of another people, watches you work all day and says: the thing that thou doest is not good. you're Moses. what do you do?
o: take his advice and share the load.
games.why: Moses listens. he appoints judges and keeps only the great cases. the advice of an outsider shapes Israel's courts.

practice: Think of someone outside your usual circle: a different generation, background, field or faith. Picture them watching you work from morning to evening, the way Yitro watched Moses, and ask what they might notice that you can't.
Let the answer surprise you if it wants to.

wordCard.voice: Yitro. Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, priest of Midian, whose advice shaped Israel's courts and whose name is on the portion of the Ten Words.

carryVoice: Your line: wisdom from outside. A week of walking now: the sign on the hand, the long way, the bones, the sea, Marah, the held-up hands. That's day three hundred forty-three.
